approach: Use s = ½at² for constant-acceleration motion from rest for both vehicles, find the time from the truck's 60 m, then find the initial gap and speeds from that time.

steps.text: Find the time for the truck to move 60 m from rest using s = ½at².
In the same time, find how far the automobile has moved from its own start.
The automobile overtakes the truck when its distance from its own start equals the truck's 60 m plus the initial gap; solve for the gap.
steps.why_this_step: Overtaking means the two vehicles are at the same absolute position, so the automobile must cover the gap plus the truck's own 60 m.

steps.text: Find the speed of each vehicle at this time using v = at.

final_answer.value: (a) t ≈ 7.39 s. (b) initial gap d ≈ 35.45 m. (c) v_truck ≈ 16.25 m/s, v_auto ≈ 25.85 m/s.

common_mistakes.text: Taking the truck's 60 m displacement itself as the initial gap between the vehicles, giving d = 60 m.
Using the automobile's own acceleration on the 60 m distance to find the time, 60 = ½(3.5)t², giving the wrong time t ≈ 5.86 s.
